cards.explanation: The answer is True. God asks why Jerusalem, the city of His people, always turns away. Then He answers it Himself: “They cling to deceit; they refuse to return.” Refuse, friends. That's not a baker who lost the recipe, that's a baker who sees the oven and walks the other way.

The answer is deceit. God says, “They cling to deceit…” Cling means a tight grip, like hanging on to the last cookie in the box while everybody stares at you. Right after that He says, “they refuse to return.”

The answer is a horse charging into battle. God says, “Everyone has pursued his own course like a horse charging into battle.” Picture that horse, friends. That's the picture God picks for everyone pursuing his own course. And in the same verse, nobody is asking, “What have I done?”

The answer is False. God says the stork, the turtledove, the swift and the thrush know when to go, “…but My people do not know the requirements of the LORD.” So the comparison is there to show the gap. A bird that never read a single word can still keep its schedule. That's the sting of it.

The answer is the lying pen of the scribes. God says “…the lying pen of the scribes has produced a deception…” The scribes were the writers, and here the pen itself is called a liar. The people said, “We are wise…” and God says that pen produced a deception. I'd be embarrassed if my stamp did that to a cookie.

The answer is word. God says, “Since they have rejected the word of the LORD, what wisdom do they really have?” They were calling themselves wise while pushing away the very thing wisdom comes from. It's like bragging about your baking while the recipe is in the trash. The word of the LORD fills the blank.

The answer is everyone from the least to the greatest. God says, “…from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain…” That's the whole ladder, bottom rung to top. Nobody gets to point at somebody else and feel clean. He adds that from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.

The answers are wound and peace. God says, “They dress the wound of the daughter of My people with very little care…” A wound needs real attention, not a quick wrap and a pat on the head. This one got the pat. The words are, “Peace, peace,” and then comes the sting: “when there is no peace at all.” They said it twice, like saying it louder would make it true. It doesn't, friends.

The answer is False. God asks if they're ashamed of the abomination they've committed. Then He says, “No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush.” A blush usually shows someone knows something is off. These folks showed nothing.

The answer is lost. God says, “Whatever I have given them will be lost to them.” That comes right after He says He will take away their harvest, with no grapes on the vine and no figs on the tree. Everything He had given them would be lost to them.

The answer is the fortified cities. The voices say, “Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there…” Fortified cities are cities built with strong defenses. That's where they propose to go, and they say they will perish there. That's a heavy line, so I think it hurts to read.

The answer is True. The voices say, “…the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.” They name the reason right there in the verse. They say it's because they have sinned against the LORD.

The answer is only terror. The voices say, “We hoped for peace, but no good has come, for a time of healing, but there was only terror.” They hoped for healing and got the opposite. That's a hard sentence, and I think it's a sad one.

The answer is horses snorting and neighing. The voices say, “The snorting of enemy horses is heard from Dan. At the sound of the neighing of mighty steeds, the whole land quakes.” Snorting and neighing are the sounds. The whole land quakes at the sound, friends. Imagine that.

The answer is that they cannot be charmed and will bite. God says, “…I will send snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you…” These vipers cannot be charmed. And they will bite. Both parts are right there in the verse.
